newsitem.title: FRANCE: George hopes alternative TARGET system not needed.
newsitem.headline: George hopes alternative TARGET system not needed.

text.p: Bank of England governor Eddie George said on Tuesday he hoped Britain would not have to go it alone on a cross-border settlement system to rival TARGET.
European Union members disagree over the degree of access to day-to-day credits under TARGET, the proposed settlement system after the introduction of a single European currency.
The Bank of England said last week it was working on alternative approaches to the TARGET system in case countries outside European monetary union were offered limited access.
"I hope that we will not reach that stage," George said in an interview with Le Figaro daily, published on Tuesday.
"We still have time to convince our partners that it is not reasonable to restrict access to TARGET to countries not participating in the euro," he said.
He added that Britain would take this line even if it decided to join in with European monetary union. Britain has said it is leaving its options open on whether or not to join.

City institutions are concerned that if Britain stays outside EMU, banks based in London will be denied access to intraday liquidity on equal terms to banks of EMU member countries and international banking business will be lost to Frankfurt or other financial centres.
Some EU members, notably France and Germany, oppose automatic equal access to intraday liquidity for EMU members and non-members.
